answer.says: Shri Hegde, the occupation is irregular, as we both know. The file is gone up for orders, and Mr. Saxena says to come after fifteen days. I do not know what to say to that, or to the fact that I have no money for a meal. I will sit in the dark for a while.
answer.thought: The evening goes on, and I sit in the dark with a man who is not me, in a house that is not mine, with six rupees that will not buy a crumb. The state is supposed to be the actuality of the ethical idea, yet here the idea has become a bureaucratic delay, a suspension in the ether where the file waits for orders that may never come. I am tired, and my body is tired, and the only thing I can do is wait for the morning to bring either the file or the end of it.
